title: What If Earth Orbited Where Mars Does?

scenes.text: What if Earth orbited where Mars does? The year gets longer, but that's not the problem.
Mars sits about 1.5 times farther from the Sun, so Earth's year would stretch to roughly 687 days.
Sunlight would drop from about 1,361 watts per square metre to roughly 586, less than half.
Without enough warmth, oceans would freeze from the top down, and ice would reflect even more sunlight.
Mars averages about minus 53 degrees Celsius, and Earth's air might hold a little heat, but not enough.
Earth wouldn't turn into Mars overnight. But the blue planet would turn white, then quiet.

description:
What if Earth orbited where Mars does?
Sunlight would fall to less than half, the year would last about 687 days, and oceans would likely freeze over.
